text:
Jules: Quick sync on mixed-capacity pools — thinking about a 'soft-reserve' on-demand band + opportunistic spot burst. How do we set min-reserve sizing and interruption handling without blowing cost targets?
Maria: Love the phrasing 'soft-reserve'. My rule of thumb: size the soft-reserve to cover p50 latency SLO for steady-state traffic, not peak. Let spot absorb tails and spikes.
Ash: Agree with Maria. Also we should classify interruptions into two buckets: 'reclaim' (very short notice) and 'evict' (longer window). Different handlers per bucket.
Sneha: Can you sketch a simple policy config we could try?
Ash: Sure — rough example: 
```
pool_policy: 
  min_on_demand: 0.25            # fraction kept available for steady qps
  burst_source: spot             # use spot for burst capacity
  burst_budget_pct: 40           # percent of total budget allowed for bursting
  interrupt_policy:
    reclaim: immediate-checkpoint
    evict: graceful-drain-60s
  cost_target: 0.70              # target fraction of work on spot
```
Sneha: Nice, that makes it concrete. For min_on_demand, do we pick by traffic percentile or by latency budget?
Maria: Pick by latency budget. Example: if p50_latency must stay <120ms, size min_on_demand so average p50 stays under that during normal shapshots (no sustained spike). Use load testing to derive multiplier for burst tolerance.
Kai: Ops note: autoscaler behavior matters — drain spot pools first, then reduce on-demand. Also consider warm on-demand shards in each AZ to avoid cross-region egress when bursting.
Maria: Cost target guidance: aim to keep 60–75% of token work on spot for typical NLP workloads. For RLHF or high-SLO use-cases raise min_on_demand to 40–50%.
ops-bot: AlertRuleCreated: interruption_rate > 5% for 10m -> notify #eng-infra @oncall
Jules: We also need graceful degradation paths — cache-first routing, shorter context, and model-tier fallback when interruption rate spikes. That reduces user-visible failures.
Ash: Implementation note: add an interruption classifier that tags events with 'latency-risk' and 'state-risk' so we pick whether we can requeue w/ prefix-KV or need immediate fallback. I'll prototype a k8s eviction hook that triggers the classifier.
Sneha: Implementation tasks I see: 1) update autoscaler to prefer draining spots, 2) build interrupt classifier + k8s hook, 3) add dashboards/alerts for interruption_rate & region-egress, 4) run chaos experiments. Who wants which?
Maria: I can take dashboards/alerts and wire the ops-bot rule.
Ash: I'll take the interrupt classifier + hook.
Jules: Can we aim for a prototype by EOD Friday? If we get the autoscaler + classifier working we can run a small chaos window. :thumbsup:
Kai: I'll run cost sims against a few workload traces (chat, embeddings, RLHF) and post numbers tomorrow. :eyes:
